name: shipment_tracking
description: Batch-checks the live carrier status of many parcels. Reads tracking numbers (one per line) from a text file, fetches each parcel's status from the carrier API, classifies the outcome, and writes one dated JSON results file with a per-outcome summary. Configurables: carrier API host http://localhost:4000/v1, input file tracking-ids.txt, delay threshold 7 days.

settings.action: Read the plain-text file at the path given by the `tracking_file` input (default `tracking-ids.txt`). Split it into lines, trim whitespace from each line, and drop blank lines. Store the cleaned values as the list `tracking_numbers` to process, and initialize an empty `results` list.
Take the next not-yet-processed tracking number from `tracking_numbers` and set it as the current `tracking_number`. This is an unattended batch run: do not ask the user anything per item.

conditions.condition: every tracking number in the list has already been processed

settings.action: Fetch the carrier status for the current parcel: GET `http://localhost:4000/v1/track?number={tracking_number}` and read the JSON response. Extract `status`, `last_location`, and `estimated_delivery` from the body. Do not stop the batch on failure — capture whatever happened so the next steps can classify it.

conditions.condition: the fetch failed, timed out, or returned a non-200 status code or an empty response body
the response indicates the tracking number was not found or is invalid
the status is out for delivery
the status is in transit and the estimated_delivery date is more than 7 days away
the status is exception, returned, or lost

settings.action: Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `error`; status, last_location, and estimated_delivery set to whatever is available (or null); and a short human-readable note explaining the carrier fetch failed or returned a bad response.

Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `not_found`; status, last_location, and estimated_delivery (or null); and a short note saying the carrier did not recognize this tracking number.
Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `delivered`; the fetched status, last_location, and estimated_delivery; and a short note confirming the parcel was delivered.

Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `out_for_delivery`; the fetched status, last_location, and estimated_delivery; and a short note saying the parcel is out for delivery / arriving today.

Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `delayed`; needs_attention set to true; the fetched status, last_location, and estimated_delivery; and a short note that the parcel is in transit but its ETA is more than 7 days away.

Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `in_transit`; the fetched status, last_location, and estimated_delivery; and a short note describing normal in-transit progress. (This is also the default for any unrecognized status.)

Append a result record for `tracking_number` with: outcome `escalate`; needs_attention set to true; the fetched status, last_location, and estimated_delivery; and a short note that the parcel hit an exception / was returned / is lost and needs manual follow-up.

All tracking numbers have been processed. Write the full `results` list as JSON to `tracking-status-<current_date>.json` (use today's date in YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. tracking-status-2026-06-21.json). At the top of the file include a summary object with the total number processed and a count per outcome (delivered, out_for_delivery, in_transit, delayed, escalate, not_found, error). Then end the flow.
